thread:
tyler: FYI customer reported 429s from Dedicated pool even though they have a 500 tps reserved shard. They say bursts go through then rapid isolation for co-tenants. Anyone seen this recently?

maria: hmm. Is this the case where multiple API keys map to the same tenant and we enforce isolation per-key vs per-tenant? :thinking:

alex: quick note — our limiter is token-bucket with an hourly replenish window for reserved throughput credits. Short bursts can consume the bucket and then we reserve isolation credits for the rest of the hour.

pranav: that sounds like intended semantics (protect steady throughput), but can surprise customers expecting short bursts to be free. Do we have telemetry showing how often this triggers on Dedicated?

infra-bot: [alert] ded_quota_isolation_triggered tenant=org-evgcorp pool=dedicated-us-east count=7 window_s=3600

june: we do; ded_quota_usage and tenant_isolation_events in datadog. But dashboards don't show "burst_credits_left" — UX gap. Customers call support confused. :eyes:

tyler: Repro steps from customer: several keys used for parallel short requests, aggregated TPS > reserved for ~20s, then next 2–3 mins see heavy 429s for other keys on same tenant. They expect short-lived spikes to be allowed up to a higher burst.

alex: config example we're currently using:```json
{
  "tenant_id": "org-evgcorp",
  "reserved_tps": 500,
  "burst_capacity": 1000,
  "replenish_window_s": 3600,
  "isolation_window_s": 3600
}
```

maria: The subtlety is replenish_window_s=3600 means burst tokens deplete and only slowly come back. If customers run many small bursts, they effectively exhaust their hourly credit. For Dedicated we probably want a shorter smoothing window or a hybrid token+leaky-bucket.

pranav: Proposal: keep protective isolation but add a short-term smoothing layer that allows transient spikes up to X for Y seconds without touching long-term credits. Something like:```
short_burst_allowance_s = 30
short_burst_mult = 3  # allow 3x reserved for 30s
```
That keeps hourly accounting accurate but reduces surprising 429s.

june: +1. Also we should make console show two metrics: "short_burst_remaining" and "hourly_credit_remaining" with labels for tenant and api_key. That will help SRE and customers debug.

tyler: Implementation caveats: need to ensure tenant isolation still prevents noisy neighbor problems. Short-burst layer must be cluster-local and bounded.

alex: Also need to define semantics for multiple API keys under same tenant: isolation enforced per-tenant, not per-key. Customer confusion comes from thinking keys are independent.

pranav: Action items: (1) add short-burst smoothing POC in limiter (2) surface "burst credits" metrics in console + datadog dashboards (3) update docs/FAQ to call out per-tenant vs per-key behavior and replenish window.

june: I'll file the dashboard tickets and mock console widget — will add a panel showing: ded_quota_hourly_pct, ded_quota_short_burst_pct, tenant_isolation_count.

tyler: I'll pair with alex for the limiter prototype. Target: small rollout to one Dedicated pool as experiment.

maria: Also add unit tests for refill math and a load test that simulates many small parallel keys under one tenant. We should validate no regressions for busy tenants.

quota-bot: Created ticket INF-4218: "short-burst smoothing for dedicated quotas" assigned to tyler,alex,june. Sprint: next.

pranav: Thanks. One more ask — add a console tooltip: "Reserved throughput is enforced per-tenant. Short bursts may be smoothed; sustained excess will consume hourly credits and trigger isolation." Small copy change could reduce support load.

tyler: Agree. I'll draft the copy. Closing loop here — will post updates in this thread when we have POC metrics.

maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
